_description: Controlled full matrix: identical source, only the CCS Optimization level changed. 3 cells x USE_LUT{0,1} x -O{off,0,1,2,3,4} = 36 measurements. Bench inference only (no sensor), MSP430G2553 @ 16 MHz.

_measurement.gru_lstm: TEST_MODE 1, host-timed over zero input, per recurrent step
_measurement.fastgrnn: run_embedded_tests 'Inference time' on real test data; per-step = window / 128, so it carries coarser run-to-run scatter than the GRU/LSTM figures (visible as non-monotonicity at some -O levels)
_measurement.hw_multiplier: --use_hw_mpy = none (MSP430G2553 has no hardware multiplier and no FPU)
_measurement.power_note: System power is flat at ~17.7 mW across all 36 runs, so energy per window scales with these latencies (E = P x t)
_measurement.flash_note: Flash was not swept; the deployed Flash figure is the production build at -O3

findings.no_lut_gain_pct: 0 to 4.6 (LSTM is flat to the last digit)
findings.lut_gain_pct: 5.5 to 8.9, saturating at -O2 for every cell
findings.mechanism: No FPU and no hardware multiplier means every float multiply/add -- and expf/tanhf -- is a precompiled TI RTS soft-float library call. The project -O level cannot change the inside of those routines; it only touches the surrounding loop and indexing glue. Tabulating the transcendentals raises the share of compilable glue, which is why -O buys a little more with LUT enabled, and why it still saturates early.
